items.headline: Hormuz disruption becomes observable as commodity-vessel transit reportedly fell to zero on Sunday
items.summary: Reuters reported on 17 August that tensions between the U.S. and Iran were materially disrupting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Commodity-vessel transit cited for Sunday fell to zero versus 31 the prior weekend, while Gulf equity markets weakened.
items.whyItMatters: This moves Hormuz from a headline-risk scenario toward an observable logistics shock. AGCI should therefore keep energy, freight and insurance as active inflation channels and preserve liquidity rather than assuming geopolitical risk is fully priced.
items.agciSignal: HORMUZ DISRUPTION / INFLATION TAIL RISK ACTIVE

items.headline: Soft U.S. data lowers near-term Fed-tightening expectations while oil remains elevated
items.summary: Global shares were steady on 17 August while the dollar fell to its weakest level since June after weaker U.S. retail sales and consumer sentiment reduced expectations for a September Fed hike. Brent advanced to about USD 89.4 and Treasury yields eased.
items.whyItMatters: The market is simultaneously pricing softer domestic demand and persistent energy risk. That combination can support duration and growth equities tactically, but it also leaves the inflation path vulnerable to a renewed oil shock.
items.agciSignal: GROWTH SOFTENING / RATE PRESSURE EASES / OIL RISK OFFSETS

items.headline: AGCI Greed rises to 91 while Valuation remains 85
items.summary: The live AGCI Greed + Valuation engine shows Greed at 91/100, Valuation at 85/100, Mid Bull regime and confidence 72/100. The model condition remains EUPHORIA_RISK with the directive 'Capital preservation / Do not chase'.
items.whyItMatters: The market remains highly complacent despite a more tangible energy and shipping shock. This divergence increases the value of cash reserves, staged entries and strict valuation discipline.
items.agciSignal: EXTREME GREED + EXTREME VALUATION / DO NOT CHASE

items.headline: Industrial production precedes FOMC minutes in this week's macro sequence
items.summary: The Federal Reserve calendar shows U.S. industrial production for 18 August and the minutes of the 28–29 July FOMC meeting for 19 August.
items.whyItMatters: Industrial production can confirm or challenge the soft-consumer narrative, while the minutes will clarify the Committee's tolerance for weaker demand versus energy-driven inflation risk.
